How the sample is built

The comparison uses the immediately preceding archived policy meeting. Both communications need a numeric score from the same stage under the same chair and quote-window convention. A missing score or missing conference breaks the sequence. The comparison also stops when the Fed switches from a target point to a range and at the listed framework and benchmark changes.

Scores run from −2 (strong easing or low-rate guidance) through 0 (an explicit steady path) to +2 (strong tightening guidance). A change records movement across these ordered categories. Distances between categories have no fixed basis-point meaning. Identical scores can include different wording or a different time horizon.

Markets supply a separate outcome. A positive rate move means the relevant futures-implied rate or swap rate rose. The Fed measure is next-meeting futures over the statement window. A one-year euro OIS spans several meetings, and the ECB press-conference window starts after the decision release. Economic information, guidance, projections and simultaneous policy action can all move prices. The quoted decisions form a historical sample with uneven coverage.

The pricing filter requires a comparable difference of at most 1 bp in absolute value between the actual policy step and the prior. Fed priors are reconstructed from the current-meeting futures surprise. ECB comparisons require a sourced, comparable deposit-rate expectation. “Policy rate unchanged” uses the archived target change at the Fed and the deposit facility rate at the ECB.
